description: The fatal open with an extended status, and the one arm of Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS that no other case reaches from the open site. OPEN INPUT at app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl:L120 reports '92', so 0000-CUSTFILE-OPEN moves 12 to APPL-RESULT at L124, takes its fatal arm at L129 and never returns. L162's condition is IF IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC OR IO-STAT1 = '9', and '92' is the interesting status precisely because it satisfies the second disjunct while failing the first: both of its bytes are digits, so a reader who checked only the class condition would predict the ELSE arm. The '9' arm holds instead, and it does not render the status as text. It passes IO-STAT1 through verbatim into IO-STATUS-04(1:1), zeroes TWO-BYTES-BINARY, moves IO-STAT2 into TWO-BYTES-RIGHT, then moves the resulting halfword into IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 - so the second character is reported as the numeric value of its byte, and the character '2' is byte 50. The line is FILE STATUS IS: NNNN9050 and not FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0092. That is the whole purpose of the TWO-BYTES-BINARY / TWO-BYTES-ALPHA redefinition at L53-L56, and a translation that simply concatenated the two status characters would pass case09 - whose numeric '35' takes the ELSE arm at L170-L172 - and fail here, which is why the two are written as a pair. SYSOUT is exactly four lines: the opening banner from L71, the error literal from L129, the rendered status from L168, and ABENDING PROGRAM from L155 immediately before CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L158. The absence of the L85 closing banner is a positive assertion rather than an omission, because the run never reaches it, and expectedReturnCode is the 12 that L124 moved into APPL-RESULT. expectedWrites, expectedFinalState and expectedDatasets are all empty for two independent reasons that both hold: CBCUS01C opens CUSTFILE INPUT and issues no WRITE and no REWRITE anywhere, and the open fails before the first READ, so no record is ever reached and there is no final state to read back. READCUST.jcl declares no PARM, so there is no job parameter. One record is nonetheless declared - row 15 of app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt, addressed as the zero-based fromRow 14 - and it is declared in order never to be read: a translation that opened lazily and read before reporting the failure would emit two extra lines, because 1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT displays at L96 and the mainline displays the same record again at L78. Those two lines per record are inherited behaviour and are kept exactly as they are (practice B5). unitKind is SERVICE: this program's decision logic lives in customer.CustomerService, which the adapter constructs with its collaborators and calls as a plain object, with no HTTP layer and no JobLauncher in the path (gate G51). It is one of the six SERVICE cases in this folder's deliberate fourteen-BATCH_JOB and six-SERVICE split, and pinning an abend through the service is what shows the fatal arm is not an artefact of the tasklet wrapper. The numeric-width rule is recorded here too, because the record this case declares and never reads is the one that carries it, and because the rule governs the key the browse itself depends on. CVCUS01Y declares exactly two PIC 9(09) spans - CUST-ID at one-based offsets 1-9 and CUST-SSN at 280-288 - and a PIC 9(n) span is zero-filled to width n where a PIC X(n) span is space-padded. CUST-ID is not merely a field: app/jcl/CUSTFILE.jcl defines the cluster with KEYS(9 0) and RECORDSIZE(500 500), so it is the nine-byte key at offset zero, and CBCUS01C browses in ascending key order through ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL with RECORD KEY IS FD-CUST-ID at L29-L33. A renderer that dropped a leading zero from a nine-digit numeric would render that key short, so it would perturb the browse ordering itself and not merely one field's bytes. On row 15 the contrast between the two fill rules is visible in adjacent spans: CUST-SSN 9(09) holds 033922034, a genuine leading-zero nine-digit value that is zero-filled, while CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID X(20) at 289-308 immediately after it holds 00000000000230369941, where the leading zeros are literal data and the span is space-padded on the right if short. Neither rule can be asserted from an image in this case, because it abends before any record exists; the width-9 assertions live where records do - case01 pins all fifty rows, and its rowIndex 14 image carries that same 033922034 at 280-288 together with CUST-ID 000000015 - while case08 pins both a field map and a full image at width 3 for CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE 001. What this case contributes is the one branch none of those can reach. CVCUS01Y declares no picture carrying a V position and CBCUS01C performs no arithmetic at all, so nothing here models a fixed-point quantity, and only the hyphenated CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD spelling of CVCUS01Y is in play (requirement I1). Provenance, practice B12: every expected value here is statically derived from the COBOL source, the CVCUS01Y byte layout, the READCUST.jcl and CUSTFILE.jcl contracts and the real app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt fixture. None of it was captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment - the substitution is the documented baseline-provenance deviation, risk R-A.
